masterText:
Arin needs to cross a dark room to get something. Arin wanted to reach the other side and get the object, but the familiar room suddenly feels strange and scary in the darkness. The old thought came quickly: "Fear means I should stop." Arin could feel the familiar room suddenly seem strange and scary once the darkness started changing what each shape felt like. Arin first froze at the edge of the dark room, letting the strange-looking shadows decide what the whole room must mean. Arin wants to stop because the fear feels like a warning. Arin then kept feeding the scary feeling in their head, and because of that the same familiar room felt less and less familiar by the second. Arin was almost ready to let the darkness choose for them and turn one crossing into something much bigger than it really was. Arin paused anyway, let the room be the same room again for a moment, and chose one next step instead of answering every shadow at once. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "It's still the same room."

Arin then chose one small brave step into the dark room, because the way through was to cross the real room in front of them rather than obey the whole scary picture in their mind. Arin acted from the new understanding that courage is taking one small brave step, instead of from the first alarm.

Arin could feel the room become more familiar again once the next step answered the darkness better than the fear had. Arin felt their body loosen and could finally breathe easier as the dark room stopped acting like a stranger.

masterText:
Arin sees a shadow under the bed and imagines a monster hiding there. Arin wanted to find out whether the monster is real and feel safe enough to sleep, but arin's imagination keeps turning ordinary shadows into frightening shapes. The old thought came quickly: "My imagination can control me." Arin could feel one shadow under the bed growing into something much bigger once imagination started filling in what could not actually be seen. Arin first stayed far from the bed, letting the hidden space underneath it decide what kind of danger must be waiting there. The more Arin imagines, the more real the fear feels. Arin then kept adding more fearful pictures in their head, and each new imagined detail made the shadow feel more real than the room around it. Arin was almost ready to let the imagined monster choose the whole night and take away the chance to find out what was actually there. Arin paused anyway, let the bed become just a bed again for one moment, and chose to face the shadow instead of the whole imagined creature at once. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "I haven't checked what it really is yet."

Arin then chose one small brave move toward the bed, because the only way to answer the fear was to meet the real shadow instead of feeding the invented monster. Arin acted from the new understanding that I can be braver than my fears, instead of from the first alarm.

Arin could feel the shadow shrink back into an ordinary shape once the brave look answered it better than imagination had. Arin felt sleep come closer once the under-bed fear lost its monster shape.

masterText:
Arin is at the doctor's office and knows an injection is coming. Arin wanted to avoid the injection or make it hurt less, but the appointment cannot simply be skipped. The old thought came quickly: "If something hurts, I can't handle it." Arin could feel the doctor visit narrowing around the coming injection, because the moment of pain had not happened yet but was already taking up too much space. Arin first tried to escape the injection in their mind, wishing the shot could somehow be skipped before it even began. Arin is afraid of pain that hasn't even happened yet.

Arin then tightened against the coming pinch, but bracing early only made the waiting chair feel longer and sharper. Arin was almost ready to let the expected pain decide the whole appointment before the shot had even happened. Arin paused anyway, listened for what was happening in the room right now, and chose to meet only the next small part of the doctor visit. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "I only have to get through the shot, not the whole future."

Arin then stayed present for the shot one brave beat at a time, because handling the real pinch was smaller than fighting the whole imagined appointment at once. Arin acted from the new understanding that I am stronger than I think, even during difficult moments, instead of from the first alarm.

Arin could feel the injection moment pass more cleanly once the fear stopped stretching it bigger than it was. Arin felt the doctor's room loosen around them once the waiting fear finally let go.

masterText: Gauri is allowed to choose one toy or treat from several appealing options. Gauri wanted to make the best choice, but each option seems exciting, and Gauri can choose only one. The old thought came quickly: "More choices always make me happier." Gauri could feel the pile of good options starting to crowd the decision instead of helping it. Gauri first tried to keep every toy or treat equally alive in their mind, afraid that choosing one would mean losing all the others. The more Gauri compares the choices, the more afraid they become of choosing the wrong one. Gauri then compared the options again and again, but more comparing only made the best choice feel harder to see. Gauri was almost ready to let the number of choices ruin the chance to enjoy any choice at all. Gauri paused, stopped trying to keep every option open, and looked for the one choice that actually fit this moment best. "Wait," Gauri told themselves. "One good choice is enough." Gauri then chose one toy or treat on purpose, because a wise choice could bring more peace than trying to hold on to everything. Gauri acted from the new understanding that wise choices matter more than having everything, instead of from the first alarm. Gauri felt the decision settle once one real choice replaced the scramble to keep every possibility. Gauri smiled once the choice finally belonged to this moment instead of all the others.

masterText:
Arin learns that they or someone close to them will need a medical procedure soon. Arin wanted to understand what will happen and feel safe, but the procedure has not happened yet, and much of it is unfamiliar. The old thought came quickly: "I won't be able to handle what's coming." Arin could feel the moment narrowing, because the feared thing was getting closer whether or not arin was ready. Arin first tried to escape it in their mind, wishing the whole moment could simply be skipped. Arin's imagination starts filling in the parts they do not understand. Arin then tried to tense against what was coming, but that only made the waiting feel sharper. Arin was almost ready to let fear decide everything about the final moment. Arin paused anyway, listened for what was actually happening now, and chose to meet only this one moment instead of the whole imagined future. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "I only have to face this part now."

Arin then held on, stayed present, and took the difficult moment one brave step at a time. Arin acted from the new understanding that I can face difficult moments one brave step at a time, instead of from the first alarm.

Arin could feel that staying with the real moment worked better than fighting a hundred imagined ones at once. Arin felt the tight waiting inside them ease, because the future had shrunk back down to one manageable moment.

masterText:
Arin sees another child being teased or treated cruelly and does not know whether or how to step in. Arin wanted to make the situation stop or help the child, but arin feels unsure, afraid, or too small to handle the situation alone. The old thought came quickly: "Speaking up won't make a difference." Arin could feel the moment closing fast, because the teasing was happening now and silence would become its own choice very soon. Arin first stayed still, hoping the cruel moment might end on its own before they had to decide anything. Arin wants to help but worries about becoming the next target. Arin then rushed through fearful possibilities in their head, but each silent second made the need to protect the other child feel sharper.

Arin was almost ready to let fear make the final choice and leave the other child alone inside the teasing. Arin paused, stopped rehearsing every worst outcome, and made room for one small brave action that could protect someone right now. "Wait," Arin told themselves. "Someone needs help now." Arin then chose the smallest real step that interrupted the cruelty, because a brave action in time mattered more than a perfect plan too late. Arin acted from the new understanding that small acts of courage can protect others, instead of from the first alarm. Arin could feel the moment change once courage turned into protection instead of staying trapped inside worry. Arin could feel relief arrive with the courage instead of after it.

masterText: Gauri discovers that a close friend has finally got the pet Gauri has always wished for. Gauri wanted to share in the excitement without feeling jealous, but the pet belongs to the friend, and Gauri cannot simply have one too. The old thought came quickly: "Life is unfair because I don't have what they have." Gauri could feel the friend's good news pulling jealousy close, because the wished-for pet made the gap between lives feel personal. Gauri first stayed fixed on the pet itself, measuring what the friend had against what they still wished for. Gauri genuinely loves the animal but finds it difficult to separate happiness for the friend from the wish that it were theirs. Gauri then let the comparison keep growing, and the more the dream pet filled the moment, the harder it became to share the friend's excitement honestly. Gauri was almost ready to let the missing pet decide that the friendship's happy moment could not also hold their own goodness. Gauri paused, noticed the jealousy without obeying it, and made room for one true thing in their own life that still deserved appreciation too. "Wait," Gauri told themselves. "Their joy is not taking mine away." Gauri then chose to share in the friend's excitement anyway, because someone else's joy did not have to cancel their own life. Gauri acted from the new understanding that I can be genuinely happy for others while appreciating my own life, instead of from the first alarm. Gauri felt the envy loosen once the friend's new pet stopped being treated like proof that life was unfair. Gauri smiled when the friendship finally felt bigger than the comparison again.
